previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with worsening low back pain and muscle spasms over two weeks, complicated by difficulty moving due to pain and recent noncompliance with lactulose. MRI showed degenerative disc disease at L5-S1 without nerve compression or cauda equina. Pain was managed with oxycodone, diazepam, tizanidine, and a lidocaine patch. Due to his history of hepatic encephalopathy, bowel regimen was intensified with lactulose, senna, and docusate to prevent constipation. He remained mentally clear throughout. No ascites was found on ultrasound. He was discharged home with a plan for outpatient physical therapy, follow-up in the chronic pain clinic, and clear instructions to avoid sedating medications if confusion develops.
problems: Degeneration of lumbar or lumbosacral intervertebral disc
Esophageal varices in diseases classified elsewhere, without mention of bleeding
Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old man with Hep C cirrhosis, grade II 
esophageal varices, presenting with abdominal and back pain 
found to have L5/S1 osteomyelitis.
.  
#. L5/S1 osteomyelitis s/p anterior and posterior fusion: The 
patient presented with back pain. CT abdomen/pelvis and MR 
___ were consistent with osteomyelitis. The began treatment 
with vancomycin and ciprofloxacin on ___, but this was 
narrowed to just vancomycin on ___. The patient underwent 
CT-guided biopsy on ___, with tissue sent for culture. The 
culture showed no growth, although the patient had already been 
on antibiotics for several days when the biopsy was done. Blood 
cultures were also negative. The spine surgery service was 
consulted and recommended anterior and posterior fusion, which 
was done in two stages. On ___, the patient underwent partial 
vertebrectomy and anterior fusion L5-S1. On ___, the patient 
underwent total laminectomy L5, laminotomy of S1, and posterior 
fusion L5-S1. The patient tolerated these procedures well. His 
pain was initially managed with a Dilaudid IV PCA. Additionally, 
an epidural catheter was placed during the posterior fusion and 
discontinued on ___. A Hemovac drain was placed during the 
posterior fusions and removed on ___. By the time of 
discharge, the patient was ambulating with assist, tolerating a 
regular diet, with pain well-controlled on oral medicatons. 
Follow-up with Dr. ___ surgery was arranged). The 
patient has a PICC (placed on ___, which can be used for 
vancomycin infusions. The patient should continue treatment with 
vancomycin 1 gm IV Q12H until ___ (6-week course). Bactrim DS 
1 tab daily can be started once course of vancomycin is 
complete. The patient will need weekly CBC, chem 10, LFTS, and 
vancomycin trough.
.
#. Acute blood loss anemia: There was some intraoperative blood 
loss requiring transfusion of a total of 4 units PRBC. The 
patient also received 7 bags of FFP and 3 bags of platelets. The 
patient's hematocrit remained stable post-operatively and 
increased appropriatedly with blood transfusions. The patient 
was prescribed ferrous sulfate to take for 1 week.
.
#. Bright red blood per rectum: The patient presented with BRBPR 
in the setting of back pain, increased opioid use, and 
constipation. The patient does have known esophageal varices, 
but the likely etiology of his bleeding was hemorrhoids. There 
was no further bleeding after admission, and the patient's 
hematocrit remained stable (except in the setting of 
intraoperative blood loss as noted above). The patient's last 
colonoscopy was on ___ and was normal to the cecum. However, 
the cecum was not fully visualized. Consideration should be 
given to repeat colonoscopy as an outpatient.
.  
#. Platelet transfusion from Rh+ donor: The platelet is Rh- and 
was transfused with Rh+ platelets on ___. The patient was 
given a dose of WinRho on ___ to prevent Rh sensitization in 
this potential liver transplant candidate.
.  
#. Acute renal failure: The patient developed acute renal 
failure, with creatinine peaking at 1.8 on ___ from baseline 
0.8. He was never oliguric. Urine sediment was bland. The 
patient's renal failure was felt to be secondary to contrast 
nephropathy. (He had a CT scan of his abdomen/pelvis on 
___. Acute interstitial nephritis was considered in the 
differential diagnosis, so ciprofloxacin was discontinued and 
omeprazole was briefly held. The patient was treated with IV 
fluids and albumin. His kidney function gradually improved, with 
creatinine 1.0 at the time of discharge. Diuretics were stopped 
in the setting of acute kidney injury but were restarted on 
___. Bactrim was also held and can be restarted once the 
patient's course of vancomycin is complete.
.  
#. Hepatitis C Cirrhosis: The patient liver function tests 
remained stable. There was no evidence of encephalopathy, 
ascites, or other decompensation. Rifaxamin, lactulose, and 
nadolol were continued. Diuretics were held in the setting of 
acute kidney injury. Lasix was started on ___, and 
spironolactone was changed to eplerenone due to gynecomastia. 
The patient should be weighed daily.
.
#. Gynecomastia: Tamoxifen was stopped in the setting of 
osteoporosis. Spironolactone was changed to eplerenone.
.  
#. Osteoporosis: Osteoporosis was noted intraoperatively by Dr. 
___ the spine surgery team. Tamoxifen was discontinued 
due to osteoporosis. Calcium and vitamin D were started. The 
patient should not receive any bisphosphonates for ___ weeks due 
to his spinal fusion.
.  
#. Psych: Continued Adderall and quetiapine.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with diffuse abdominal pain and diarrhea, to
assess for diverticulitis.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis ___ and an MR of the
abdomen ___. MR ___ study of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images of the abdomen and pelvis were acquired after
administration of intravenous contrast.  Oral contrast was not administered. 
Sagittal and coronal reformats were generated and reviewed.

FINDINGS:  Bilateral basal small pleural effusions and associated adjacent
basal atelectasis are new since the prior study.  Multiple calcified nodules
in the left lung base suggestive of prior granulomatous disease. The heart and
pericardium appear unremarkable.

The liver demonstrates a nodular contour, consistent with cirrhosis.  In this
single-phase contrast-enhanced study, no suspicious liver lesions are
detected.  There is minimal pneumobilia without dilation of the intra- or
extra-hepatic biliary tree.  The patient is status post cholecystectomy.  The
portal vein is patent.  Enlarged splenic hilum and splenorenal collaterals are
seen.  Both adrenal glands are normal.  Both kidneys show symmetric
opacification and excretion of contrast without evidence of hydronephrosis or
renal masses.  The spleen is enlarged measuring 18.1 cm (400B:42) and has
multiple calcified densities suggestive of prior granulomatous disease
exposure.  Pancreas enhances homogeneously, but there is haziness of the
peripancreatic fat .  This could be seen in patients with portal hypertension.
However, in the appropriate clinical setting, this could represent early acute
pancreatitis.  Stomach and small bowel appear unremarkable without evidence of
bowel wall thickening, obstruction, or mass lesions.  There is no free air
within the abdomen.  There is minimal free fluid in the perihepatic region and
in the pelvis.  No significant retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy
is detected.  Celiac artery and the superior mesenteric artery, the superior
mesenteric vein and splenic vein are all patent.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:  The bladder is distended and
appears unremarkable.  The prostate gland and seminal vesicles are
unremarkable.  The rectum and sigmoid colon are normal without evidence of
diverticulitis or diverticulosis.  No significant pelvic lymphadenopathy is
seen.  There is minimal free fluid layering in the pelvis.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES AND SOFT TISSUES:  In comparison to the prior study, there
is new erosion of the vertebral endplates at L5-S1 level with endplate
destruction.  There is associated soft tissue swelling extending from the
intervertebral space to the prevertebral region with associated fat stranding
in the region.  These findings are highly suggestive of discitis with
osteomyelitis at L5-S1 level.  No other suspicious bone lesions are detected.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Cirrhosis of the liver.
2.  Splenomegaly, extensive varices and minimal ascites - indicative of portal
hypertension.
3..  Erosion of the inferior endplate of L5 and superior endplate of S1 with
prevertebral soft tissue stranding, consistent with discitis and osteomyelitis
at L5-S1 level.  This is new since the prior MR ___ study of ___.
3.  ___ fat stranding, could be related to portal hypertension.
However, in the appropriate clinical setting, this may be a picture of acute
pancreatitis.

The findings were discussed with Dr. ___ at 10:30 a.m. on ___.

INDICATION:  Back pain.  Abdominal and pelvic CT scan performed on ___, due to diffuse abdominal pain and diarrhea, demonstrates new erosion of
the L5-S1 endplates, concerning for osteomyelitis.

COMPARISON:  Lumbar spine MRI without contrast dated ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and STIR images of the lumbar
spine, with axial T1- and T2-weighted images.  Following intravenous
gadolinium administration, sagittal and axial T1-weighted images were
repeated.

FINDINGS:  There is new edema and contrast enhancement in the anterior aspect
of the L5-S1 intervertebral disc.  There is increased extent of edema in the
L5-S1 endplate compared to ___, with associated contrast enhancement. 
Given the presence of endplate erosion at this level on the preceding
abdominal/pelvic CT scan, this indicates new osteomyelitis superimposed on
preexisting discogenic bone marrow changes.  There is anterior paravertebral
contrast enhancement spanning L5 and S1, consistent with a phlegmon, measuring
5 mm in maximal width.  There is no evidence of an enhancing epidural
collection.  A disc bulge and a small central/right paracentral disc
protrusion are again seen at this level, contacting the traversing S1 nerve
roots.  Mild facet arthropathy is also present.  Mild right and moderate left
neural foraminal narrowing is again seen.

Vertebral body height and alignment are normal.  The conus medullaris
terminates at T12-L1.  There is no pathologic leptomeningeal enhancement. 
Mild disc bulges are again seen from L2-3 through L4-5.  Facet joint
arthropathy is again noted at L3-4 and L5-S1, with fluid in the facet joints. 
There is unchanged mild neural foraminal narrowing at L4-5.  There is no
significant spinal canal narrowing.

No signal abnormalities are detected in the imaged retroperitoneal soft
tissues.

IMPRESSION:
1.  New discitis and osteomyelitis at L5-S1, with a small anterior
paravertebral phlegmon.  No evidence of epidural phlegmon or abscess.

2.  Unchanged multilevel spondylosis.

BIOPSY:

HISTORY: This is a ___ y/o man with a history of low back pain found on MRI and
CT to have discitis and osteomyelitis, the tissue biopsy for spine pain.
Patient has a history of cirrhosis and hepatitis C. 

ATTENDING: Dr. ___.

ASSISTANT: Dr. ___ fellow.

TECHNIQUE: Following the full discussion of the risks and benefits of the
procedure as well as alternative management, written informed consent to
perform spine biopsy at L5-S1 was obtained. Patient was brought to the
fluoroscopic suite and placed in prone position on the fluoroscopic table.
Patient was prepared in a standard sterile fashion and superficially
anesthetized with 1% Lidocaine. Under fluoroscopic guidance, approach to
access the disc space at the level of L5-S1 on the left side using a 22 gauge
spinal needle was then performed. Core biopsy needle was advanced into the
disc space.

A 22 gauge ___ needle was used and samples were obtained x 2. After the
procedure, the biopsy needle was withdrawn, patient tolerated the procedure
well and there were no complications. 

Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of Fentanyl 150
mcg and Versed 1.5 mg for a total interservice time of 30 minutes during which
time the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored.

IMPRESSION: Successful disc space biopsy of L5/S1. Samples were sent to
microbiology as requested by the referring physician.
